title: String methods
lede: The String surface is nearly complete. Comparison and substring search are binary-safe (length-headed, NUL-tolerant); the open edges are real Unicode — normalization, surrogate-pair code points, and locale collation — which this compiler has no tables for and does not fake.

entries.name: + (concatenation)
entries.description: Joins two strings. A null operand stringifies as "null", matching JavaScript — including a `number | null` held in a parameter, a local, an object field, or returned from a function.

entries.name: .length
entries.description: The number of bytes in the string. This compiler's strings are byte sequences, so for ASCII/Latin-1 text this equals the character count.

entries.name: .slice(start, end?)
entries.description: Returns a section of the string without mutating the original. Negative indices count from the end.

params.name: start
params.desc: Zero-based start index; negative counts from the end.

params.name: end?
params.desc: Exclusive end index; defaults to the string length.

entries.snippet:
console.log('Hello, World!'.slice(7, 12))   // World
console.log('Hello, World!'.slice(-6))      // orld!

entries.name: .substring(start, end?)
entries.description: Like slice, but negative arguments clamp to 0 and a start greater than end is swapped, matching JavaScript.

params.name: start
params.desc: Start index; clamped to 0 if negative.

params.name: end?
params.desc: Exclusive end index; defaults to the string length.

returns.desc: A new string between the two indices.

entries.snippet:
console.log('Hello, World!'.substring(0, 5))   // Hello
console.log('Hello, World!'.substring(5, 0))   // Hello   (swapped)

entries.name: .indexOf(substr)
entries.description: Returns the byte index of the first occurrence of the substring, or -1 if absent. Binary-safe past an embedded NUL.

entries.name: .includes(substr)
entries.description: Whether the string contains the substring. Binary-safe (searches with memmem over a length header).

returns.desc: true if the substring is present.

entries.name: .startsWith(prefix)
entries.description: Whether the string begins with the prefix. Returns false when the string is shorter than the prefix.

returns.desc: true if the string starts with the prefix.

entries.name: .endsWith(suffix)
entries.description: Whether the string ends with the suffix. Returns false when the string is shorter than the suffix.

returns.desc: true if the string ends with the suffix.

entries.name: .replace(from, to)
entries.description: Replaces the first occurrence of `from` with `to`, returning the original string when there is no match. See RegExp for regex-pattern edges.

returns.desc: A new string with the first match replaced.

entries.name: .split(sep)
entries.description: Splits the string on a separator into an array. An empty separator splits into individual characters, matching JavaScript.

entries.name: .trim()
entries.description: Strips leading and trailing whitespace. Uses the full JS WhiteSpace/LineTerminator set (U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000–200A, U+2028/29, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000, U+FEFF — UTF-8-aware), not just ASCII.

entries.name: .trimStart() / .trimEnd()
entries.description: Strips whitespace from one side only, using the same full whitespace set as trim().

entries.name: .toString()
entries.description: Identity on a string, matching JavaScript. Kept because Node code habitually calls it on values that are Buffers there but strings here (spawnSync results, stream chunks).

entries.name: .toUpperCase()
entries.description: Returns the string with ASCII letters uppercased.

entries.name: .toLowerCase()
entries.description: Returns the string with ASCII letters lowercased.

entries.name: .repeat(n)
entries.description: Returns the string repeated n times.

entries.name: .padStart(len, pad?)
entries.description: Pads the start of the string to a target length. An empty pad string is a no-op, matching JavaScript.

params.name: pad?
params.desc: Pad string; defaults to a space.

entries.name: .padEnd(len, pad?)
entries.description: Pads the end of the string to a target length. Same empty-pad rule as padStart.

params.name: pad?
params.desc: Pad string; defaults to a space.

entries.name: .charCodeAt(i)
entries.description: Returns the byte-space code unit at index i. Bounds-checked: an out-of-range index (negative or >= length) returns NaN, as real JS — the result is a double for exactly that reason.

returns.desc: The code unit, or NaN if out of range.

entries.name: .at(i)
entries.description: Returns the character at index i, with negative indices counting from the end.
differences: An out-of-range `i` returns `""` rather than real JS's `undefined` — deterministic and safe, but a real string a caller could mistake for actual data.

entries.name: .charAt(i)
entries.description: Returns the character at index i. Never wraps a negative index from the end — always "" for any out-of-range i, matching real JS's distinction from .at().

returns.desc: The character at i, or "" if out of range.

entries.name: .codePointAt(i)
entries.description: Returns the code point at index i.

returns.desc: The code point, or NaN if out of range.

differences: This compiler's strings are plain byte sequences, not real UTF-16 — no surrogate-pair/multi-byte decoding, so this is exactly `.charCodeAt(i)`'s byte value under a second name; correct only for ASCII/Latin-1 text.
An out-of-range index returns `NaN` (bounds-checked), where real JS returns `undefined` — no undefined sentinel for a numeric result.

entries.name: .normalize()
entries.description: Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD). Deliberately deferred, not attempted — it needs real Unicode normalization tables this compiler has no infrastructure for; a fake identity-only implementation would silently mis-normalize any non-ASCII composed/decomposed text.

entries.name: .match() / .matchAll()
entries.signature: match(re: RegExp): string[] | null; matchAll(re: RegExp): string[][]
entries.description: PCRE2-backed regex matching. .match() is real-JS-shaped. See RegExp for the full pattern-language caveats.
differences: `.matchAll()` returns an eager `string[][]` rather than a lazy iterator.

entries.name: .search(pattern)
entries.description: Searches for a pattern and returns its index, or -1. A plain-string pattern is coerced to a RegExp exactly as in real JS (metacharacters are interpreted — `'a.b'.search('.')` is 0), and a RegExp pattern runs a real PCRE2 search.

entries.name: .replaceAll(from, to)
entries.description: Replaces every non-overlapping occurrence of `from` with `to`. An empty search is JS-faithful — `'abc'.replaceAll('', '-')` is `'-a-b-c-'`.

returns.desc: A new string with all matches replaced.

entries.name: .localeCompare(other)
entries.description: Compares two strings, returning exactly -1, 0, or 1. Binary-safe past an embedded NUL.
differences: Length-aware byte-order comparison, not real Unicode collation — no locale/`Intl` infrastructure.

entries.name: String.fromCharCode(n)
entries.description: Builds a string from one or more byte-space code units. Static method on String.

entries.name: String.fromCodePoint(n)
entries.description: Builds a string from code points. In this compiler's byte-space strings this is a BMP alias of fromCharCode.

entries.name: String.raw tag
entries.description: The String.raw tag interleaves the raw (undecoded) quasi text with the string-coerced interpolations — escape sequences appear verbatim (String.raw`a\nb` is a\nb), byte-for-byte the same as Node.
